name: Westchester Lagoon (Margaret Eagan Sullivan Park)
rentals: free kids' skates at Saturday Family Skate (2026); no adult rental found
notes: The city's main outdoor skating spot. Groomed only once ice is at least 12 in. It then has an open skate area, 2 hockey rinks and a ~1/4-mile oval around the small islands on the north shore. When conditions allow you can skate more than 1 mile around the shoreline. Burn barrels and firewood are provided. Saturday Family Skate runs 1–3pm, typically January–February, so it probably starts after the trip. Opening dates vary a lot: 27 Nov 2024 (12–14 in), 10 Dec 2021 (13 in), but in late Dec 2023 the ice was only 8 in and it opened in January. Ice never forms at the inflow and outflow, so stay in the groomed area.

name: Cuddy Family Midtown Park – speed-skating oval + skate pond
area: Anchorage – Midtown (201 E 40th Ave, by Loussac Library)
maintainedBy: MOA Parks & Rec; volunteer group Anchorage Skates
notes: 400 m outdoor long-track oval, one of only a handful in the US, and usually the smoothest outdoor ice in town. The oval is flooded, so it can open before the lakes. The separate skate pond is an MOA-maintained skating zone once ice is 12 in. A PA system plays music.

name: Delaney Park Strip hockey & figure rinks
surface: flooded (hot-mopped daily when conditions allow, per 2018)
notes: Walkable from downtown. Rinks can be reserved through Active Communities, so pickup hockey may take the ice.

name: Town Square Park rink
lit: holiday lights in park; rink lighting ?
notes: Small seasonal rink in the downtown core, revived in 2020. In January 2025 it was described as a 'work in progress' with few skaters. Holiday lights and ice sculptures in the park. Status for 2026-27 is unknown.

name: Bonnie Cusack outdoor rinks #1/#2 (Chester Creek Sports Complex / Mulcahy)
coordNote: approx (sports-complex centroid; Bonnie Cusack not in Nominatim)
maintainedBy: MOA; reservations via Alpine Services (907-441-0586); Anchorage Skate Club rents ice
notes: Next to Ben Boeke and Sullivan Arena. Open skating is often unavailable because of permitted or reserved events.

name: Tikishla Park (Scotty Gomez) hockey rink
notes: The rink where NHL player Scott Gomez learned. Open in late Nov 2024. Hockey practices and games can block open skating.

name: Chanshtnu Muldoon Park skating ribbon
notes: A skating path (ribbon) through the park, regularly maintained. Open in late Nov 2024.

name: Cheney Lake
notes: Maintained skating zone (open area, hockey rinks, ribbon) once ice is 12 in. It usually opens after Westchester. Recurring overflow problem with unknown cause.

name: Goose Lake
area: Anchorage – UAA/U-Med (3220 E Northern Lights; access north end of UAA Dr)
notes: Listed as an MOA-maintained skating zone in 2025, but it tends to open later in the season. Connects to the Chester Creek trail.

name: Jewel Lake
notes: An older MOA memo lists it as maintained at 12 in, but in 2018 it was only measured and it is not on the 2025 list. When the ground is frozen you can sometimes walk or skate between Jewel, Sundi and Sand lakes.

name: DeLong Lake
notes: Alaska.org lists it among maintained lakes, but it is not on the 2025 MOA list. Treat it as unmaintained unless the MOA status report says otherwise.

name: Wasilla Lake city rink
coordNote: approx (Newcomb Park point on Wasilla Lake)
notes: About 1 acre of the lake, opened once ice is about 11 in. No restrooms. The source article's date is unclear and may be old, so check with the City of Wasilla.

name: Wonderland Park rink
notes: About 75x75 ft, unenclosed and self-policed, with restrooms nearby. Described as 'planned' in an article of uncertain date, so it may not exist now.

name: Alyeska Resort holiday rink
notes: Only a past holiday event was found. Whether there is a rink in 2026 is unconfirmed, so contact the resort.

name: Campbell Lake
notes: Largest lake in Anchorage. It is shallow, so it freezes early. Access is via 2 public easements between homes, or a small lot north of Dimond Blvd when the inflow is frozen. Officially confirmed as a public lake. Test the ice yourself.

name: Sand Lake
notes: Good size, easy access and an interesting shoreline. Can be linked with Jewel and Sundi lakes when the ground is frozen.

name: Taku Lake (Taku-Campbell Park)
notes: Small park lake. No skating information was found in any source, so treat it as unmaintained.

name: Little Campbell Lake (Kincaid Park)
notes: Small lake ringed by wooded hills in the NE corner of Kincaid Park. Kincaid's groomed ski trails are next to it.

name: Potter Marsh
notes: Roadside maze of lagoons and reedy channels, with better ice than the rest of the coastal refuge. Very variable, with open holes from marsh gas. Popular and can get crowded.

name: Anchorage Coastal Wildlife Refuge (via Oceanview Bluff Park; Woronzof/Kincaid lagoons)
coordNote: approx (refuge centroid; Oceanview Bluff Park not in Nominatim)
notes: From Oceanview Bluff Park, walk down the sled hill and about 0.5 mi to the coast, then skate among stranded icebergs. The ice is usually thin and inconsistent, and salt and silt dull blades. Extreme tides: stay close to shore.

name: Lake Spenard
maintainedBy: Alaska DOT&PF (part of Lake Hood Seaplane Base)
notes: Do not skate here. It is an active aircraft operating area (ski planes, engine run-ups), and the airport's pedestrian guidance says 'Stay off the ice'. No public skating permission was found. Spenard Beach Park is on the shore. Airport Ops 907-266-2600.

name: Lake Hood
notes: Closed. The airport says Lake Hood is closed to pedestrians year-round and walking on the ice is not permitted. In winter the ice is used by ski-equipped aircraft.

name: Mirror Lake
maintainedBy: ER/Chugiak Parks (2018: rink provided but no ice maintenance)
notes: Small shallow lake, about 1.5 mi around. The Mirror Lake winter loop around the lake is occasionally groomed, and the Coyote ski trails are nearby. ER/Chugiak Parks: 907-343-1500.

name: Rabbit Lake (and McHugh Lake)
notes: 4.3-mile walk from the Rabbit Lake Trailhead. Clear alpine lake with underwater boulder gardens, best known Oct–Nov before snow. By late December it is usually snow-covered. Mountain terrain: check avalanche conditions.

name: Eagle & Symphony Lakes
area: Chugach State Park – South Fork Eagle River
notes: About a 4.8–5 mi hike from the South Fork trailhead. The drive time is approximate because the trailhead was not geocoded. Symphony is clear and Eagle is opaque turquoise. They are early-season alpine lakes and usually snowed over by late December. Avalanche terrain.

name: Eklutna Lake
area: Chugach State Park – north (end of Eklutna Lake Rd)
notes: 3,200 acres and the only road-accessible lake in Chugach SP. It freezes out of step with other lakes because of its size and elevation. Wind can clear the surface or roughen it. Glare ice draws crowds (e.g. Jan 2025). When snowed in, it is good for crust or frost skiing and ski-touring across the lake. Ice thinned to under 1 in during a warm spell one February.

name: Portage Lake
area: Portage Valley / Turnagain Arm (Begich-Boggs Visitor Center)
notes: About 3 mi of skating to the Portage Glacier face, over a 600-ft-deep lake. Slow to freeze and may not freeze at all in warm winters. Pressure ridges, leads, and thin ice where there was recently open water. Calving sends waves under the ice: in Feb 2025 two skaters were stranded and rescued by helicopter. Keep well back from the face and stay off icebergs. Avalanche and rockfall risk from the side slopes. No cell service. USFS wants at least 4 in of clear new ice. USFS Girdwood: 907-783-3242.

name: Twentymile Lagoons
coordNote: approx (Twentymile River point; lagoons are near the highway)
notes: Roadside lagoon networks north and south of the river. Wind-blown silt, thin ice in the passageways, and gas holes throughout. Turnagain Arm weather swings between chinook wind, rain and deep cold.

name: Placer River lagoons
notes: Large roadside lagoon among salt-killed 'ghost' trees, with smaller lagoons linked several miles up the valley. Silt and wind.

name: Lynx Lake Loop (Nancy Lake SRA)
coordNote: Lynx Lake point; summer start Tanaina Lake 61.670233,-150.09378
notes: 8-mile canoe loop linking 14 lakes, with portages up to 0.5 mi. Inland lakes freeze before coastal ones. Skateable only after freeze-up and before significant snow. In winter the parkway is not plowed past the mile 2.2 Winter Trailhead, so the usual Tanaina lot start may not be reachable by car. Public-use cabins on Lynx Lake.

name: Rabbit Slough & Wasilla Creek (Palmer Hay Flats)
area: Palmer Hay Flats State Game Refuge (Glenn Hwy)
notes: Miles of frozen channels and ponds, with lagoons about 5.5 mi out and moose on the flats. Wind often keeps it nearly snow-free, so the season lasts longer than elsewhere: one of the better late-December bets. Watch for overflow, very variable thickness and glacial silt. Sometimes you can loop down Rabbit Slough and back up Wasilla Creek.

name: Jim Creek / Mud Lake / Jim–Swan lakes / Knik River sloughs
coordNote: approx (Jim Lake point; Mud Lake start not geocoded)
notes: Tours run 20–31 mi from Mud Lake down Jim Creek to the Knik River. Overflow can make smooth 'art gallery' ice. The creek and the glacial, braided Knik River are moving water, with the highest break-through risk. Knik Glacier lagoon needs off-road or air access.

name: Reflections Lake
notes: Easy roadside access. Narrow passageways at the far end give 'adventure skating' when conditions allow.

name: Lake Lucille
maintainedBy: none on ice (Lake Lucille Park run by Mat-Su Borough)
notes: Bigger than Wasilla Lake, with several access points. Lake Lucille Park has 2.5 km of perimeter trails for skiing and skijoring.

name: Finger Lake
notes: The most heavily stocked lake in the Valley and a busy ice-fishing lake. No skating reports found. Watch for auger holes.

name: Matanuska Lakes SRA (Kepler-Bradley: Matanuska, Kepler, Bradley, Canoe, Irene, Long lakes)
notes: Among the most heavily ice-fished lakes in the Valley. Long Lake Loop is a popular cross-country ski trail. Connects to the Crevasse-Moraine trails. No skating reports found.

name: Big Lake
maintainedBy: none (Big Lake Trails Inc. maintains snowmachine trails)
notes: The Valley's snowmachine hub, with high-speed machine traffic on the ice. Large lake, so expect pressure ridges and variable ice. No skating-specific information found.

name: Upper Trail Lake (Moose Pass; also Tern & Summit lakes)
notes: Park at the salmon hatchery lot, cross the Moose Creek bridge and scramble down to the ice. Freezes long before Kenai Lake. About 2 h, at the edge of the range.

name: Skilak Lake
notes: Beyond 2 h (probably about 2.5 h; the routing estimate was unreliable). Very large lake with leads, pressure ridges and variable ice.

name: Nancy Lake SRA Winter Trailhead (lake & ski routes)
coordNote: approx (Nancy Lake Parkway road point, not the trailhead itself)
surface: snow on lake ice; groomed ski-only trails
notes: About 40 mi of winter trails, including ~10 mi groomed ski-only, though one user reports parts are snowmachine-packed rather than groomed. The 6–7 mi route to the Lynx Lake cabins follows the unplowed parkway and crosses several frozen lakes, so it is a classic snowy-lake ski tour. Reservable cabins on Lynx, Red Shirt, James, Nancy and Bald lakes. Nancy Lake itself: 61.690529,-150.01464.

name: Beach Lake Park (Nordic trails + lake)
maintainedBy: ER/Chugiak Parks; grooming by Chugiak-Eagle River Nordic Ski Club
notes: 15+ km of groomed classic and skate trails. The lake itself is open for ice fishing only and is not maintained for skating (2018).

name: Byers Lake (Denali State Park)
maintainedBy: Alaska State Parks (no winter trail maintenance)
notes: Outside the 2-hour range (about 3+ h). The campground road is unplowed: park at the Alaska Veterans Memorial (mile 147.1) and ski 0.9 mi to the day-use area. Public-use cabins. Ski touring and ice fishing.
